rows.fact: OpenShell v0.1.2's Landlock ruleset grants LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_REFER on every read_write path (its sandbox crate adds each read_write rule with AccessFs::from_all at ABI V3), so under plimsoll's policy (/tmp read-write, hard_requirement) a session's code, and any process it starts in the background, can rename(2) a folder or a file from /tmp/work to elsewhere under /tmp, hard-link a file out of it, and rename /tmp/work itself or move it under a new folder: all allowed, none EXDEV. Landlock is in force there (a world-readable /var outside the policy is refused), the kernel's Landlock ABI seen inside is 7 (errata 15), and a nested domain without REFER does refuse the same rename with EXDEV, so Landlock does not keep a folder inside the work folder on OpenShell; only a mount of its own would.
